A reading is valid when it is between 0 and 100 inclusive. Invalid readings break a run and cannot belong to one. Within a stable run, the absolute difference between every pair of neighbouring readings must be at most 3, inclusive. When two valid neighbours differ by more than 3, the later reading may start a new run of length 1. Do not remove invalid entries and join readings across the resulting gap. Return 0 for an empty array or an array with no valid readings. A single valid reading counts as a run of length 1. Leave the input array unchanged. No input-reading code, printing, class wrapper, or particular time complexity is required; only the method's return value is assessed.

Examples: [10, 12, 15, -1, 30, 34, 35, 36] returns 3; [4, 8, 11] returns 2; [0, 3, 6, 100] returns 3; [101, -1] returns 0. The range endpoints and a difference of exactly 3 are allowed.
